item.title: Tailoring Cathode Interphase with Cyclic Ethers toward Stable Lithium‐Metal Batteries
item.description:

ENERGY & ENVIRONMENTAL MATERIALS | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This work reveals that cyclic ether ring structure controls ring-opening thermodynamics and cathode interphase chemistry in lithium-metal batteries. Comparing DOL and DOX shows distinct interfacial pathways: DOL enables stable LiFePO₄ cycling, while DOX stabilizes high-voltage NCM811. The findings establish interfacial reactivity matching as a design principle for tailoring ether electrolytes, advancing durable lithium-metal batteries.

💡 This work shows that activating selenium anionic redox overcomes phase-selectivity limits in copper selenide cathodes, converting zincophobic CuSe into a high-capacity electrode (4 to 413 mAh g⁻¹, doubled voltage, 4000-cycle life). It enables the whole CuySe family as stable zinc-battery cathodes and generalizes to other nucleophilic additives, revitalizing a dormant material class.

It reveals that carbonaceous residues from PVDF/separator interact with NCM surfaces, forming oxygen-rich coatings along grain boundaries that block lithium diffusion and cut recovery below 80%.
